songs.lyrics:
[Intro]
Play the Old Record

[Verse 1: Male Vocal]
I press the shirt across the kitchen table,
and check the collar twice beneath the lamp.
The record in the next room turns slowly,
and every song makes Saturday come near.
I have been waiting all week for this evening,
though I pretend it is nothing much at all.

[Chorus: Male and Female Duet]
The week grows small when the first song starts,
and every mirror gives the room a glow.
Leave the needle where the good part finds us,
Play the Old Record.

[Verse 2: Female Vocal]
I pin my hair and change my shoes again,
then hear your car before it reaches home.
I laugh because the nerves have made me foolish,
and one low harmony answers from the hall.
The dance has not begun, but something has,
and I can feel it in the waiting.

[Bridge: Male and Female Call and Response]
One more turn before we leave.
One more breath before the door.

[Chorus: Male and Female Duet]
The old room holds the little things we practice,
the smile, the coat, the courage to step out.
Keep the needle moving while we finish,
Play the Old Record.

[Final Chorus: Male and Female Duet Harmony]
Play the Old Record,
let the low harmony stay close beside us.
No need to rush the night before it starts,
we have all evening waiting at the door,
Play the Old Record.

songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The summer hall was warmer than the garden,
and every chair had coats across the back.
You asked if I would dance before I answered,
then waited while I tried to find my hands.
The room looked larger from the edge of music,
until your shoulder gave my hand a place.

[Pre-Chorus]
One slow step, then another,
and the floor became less frightening.

[Chorus]
I could hear my own heart over everything,
but you never asked me to move fast.
You only smiled and turned me toward the doorway,
Walk the Garden Path.

[Verse 2]
We slipped outside when the room grew crowded,
and summer roses leaned along the fence.
Your sleeve brushed mine beside the gravel,
and neither one of us stepped farther off.
That first small certainty has stayed for years,
not loud enough to fade away.

[Bridge]
One chord darkens, then the warm key returns,
like a shy thought finally spoken.

[Chorus]
The dance inside kept moving without us,
but our slower rhythm suited me.
You held the gate and waited in the moonlight,
Walk the Garden Path.

[Final Chorus]
Walk the Garden Path,
let the old summer move at its own speed.
One shy hand, one shoulder, one sure answer,
that was enough to tell me what I knew,
Walk the Garden Path.

songs.lyrics:
[Intro]
We Made It Through

[Verse 1]
The map is open crooked on the dashboard,
and sunset runs along the passenger door.
We missed the turn about ten miles behind us,
but neither one suggests we turn around.
The radio is low, the road is nearly empty,
and every mile feels kinder than the last.

[Chorus]
We never knew exactly where we were going,
and that became the best part of the view.
The day went down, the road kept carrying us,
We Made It Through.

[Verse 2]
A service station glows beside the highway,
we buy two drinks and ask how far the coast is.
The answer does not matter like it used to,
because the evening has already won.
You fold the map and leave it on your knees,
and I keep driving slowly into blue.

[Chorus]
No timetable could tell us what was waiting,
no fixed arrival made the sky more true.
The miles grew calm, and so did we beside them,
We Made It Through.

[Final Chorus]
We Made It Through,
not by hurrying, not by knowing everything.
The road kept opening under a quiet sunset,
and you were there each time I looked across,
We Made It Through.

songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The porch step warms beneath the afternoon,
and every truck makes me look down the road.
You promised there would be a letter coming,
though you could not say exactly when.
I keep the radio beside the window,
low enough to hear the tires outside.

[Chorus]
The announcer talks between two old slow records,
and I let another hour move along.
If the mail is late, I can still keep waiting,
Keep the Radio Playing.

[Verse 2]
Three houses down, a screen door opens,
and someone gathers sheets from off the line.
At last a white truck turns into the street,
and my heart moves faster than my feet.
The envelope is thin, your writing unmistakable,
and suddenly the whole porch feels like spring.

[Bridge]
One quiet hum meets one piano answer.
Nothing else needs saying for a while.

[Chorus]
I read the first line twice before the second,
and hear your voice inside the careful words.
Now the waiting has somewhere to rest,
Keep the Radio Playing.

[Final Chorus]
Keep the Radio Playing,
let the slow song finish while I read.
The letter came without a grand arrival,
but every line has brought you close again,
Keep the Radio Playing.

songs.lyrics:
[Intro]
Stay a While, Darling

[Verse 1]
The city lights come on in little clusters,
and traffic turns to ribbons down below.
Two folding chairs sit near the rooftop railing,
just far enough apart to move them close.
You hand me half the blanket from your shoulder,
and the whole Sunday seems to slow at once.

[Chorus]
There is nowhere else that needs us now,
and no last train we have to run to catch.
Let the lights come on without us leaving,
Stay a While, Darling.

[Verse 2]
A taxi horn dissolves between the buildings,
and one window after another turns to gold.
You ask which house was mine when I was younger,
I point toward a block I cannot quite see.
Then I remember carrying a chair at supper,
and how a street can make a person home.

[Breakdown]
We sit without filling every silence,
and that is how I know the night is kind.

[Chorus]
The city does not need another answer,
it only needs these lights and both of us.
Move your chair a little closer to me,
Stay a While, Darling.

[Final Chorus]
Stay a While, Darling,
the first porch lights are somewhere down below.
Tomorrow we can carry chairs and stories,
but tonight leave one small ending open,
Stay a While, Darling.
